title: One backward row
statement: Let $I$ be an index type, let $f$ assign a payload to each integer coordinate and index, let $d$ assign a direction in $\{-1,0,1\}$ to each index, and let $z\in\mathbb Z$. Applying the backward row transducer with right register $f(z+1)$ to the cached row at $z$ gives register $f(z)$ and the uncached row whose payload at coordinate $z$ and index $i$ is $f(z+d(i),i)$.
replaced:
For every payload family $f$, every vector of directions $d$, and every coordinate
$z$, applying the backward transducer with directions $d$ and register the payloads at
$z + 1$ to the cached row at $z$ produces the payloads at $z$ as the new register
together with the uncached row at $z$ of the shifted family sending coordinate $z$ and
tape $i$ to the value of $f$ at $z$ plus the direction of $i$.
